The cancellation identity is derived in the paper's order: the unit substitution, then tensoring to RF^+R=F^+, then commuting the permutation with the pointwise product, then the convolution rule and the normalization. The conjugation remark that supplies RF_s^+ is also given.
The page writes out the sum and the substitution w'=beta w, giving (1/q)sum z_{w'} e^{2 pi i w' beta^{-1} j/q} = (R_beta^{-1}F_q^+z)_j, which is correct and the same as the paper's h=ck step.

The normalized convolution rule F_s(u*v)=S(F_su).(F_sv) is quoted, not shown, which is also how the paper treats it. F_s^+F_s=I/S follows from the stated F_q^+F_q=I/q by tensoring ("Hence"). Both normalizations are correct.
The page combines the two normalizations: "(1/S)F_s^+F_s(u*v)=u*v/S^2", which matches the paper.

errors.quote: Take $d$ axes with pairwise coprime prime lengths $s_i$ and power-of-two lengths $t_i>s_i$ ... Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$
errors.problem: t_i is a unit modulo s_i only when s_i is odd, and the page's setup allows s_i=2. The resampling lemma requires gcd(s,t)=1, and the paper chooses "distinct odd primes" and notes "Every gcd(s_i,t_i) equals one because t_i is a power of two."

errors.quote: where $*$ is the [cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$
errors.problem: The convolution is d-dimensional cyclic convolution on the product of the groups Z/t_i, which has T entries. The paper says "cyclic convolution on the product of the coordinate groups". Because the t_i are powers of two, this group is not Z/T for d>=2, so "of length T" read as one-dimensional is inaccurate.

errors.quote: Both maps are applied one line at a time, so errors and times add over the d axes: error below $dp^2$
errors.problem: The page never gives the per-line error bound p^2 of the one-dimensional algorithms (its one-axis paragraph lists only the identity and the time). It also does not say that within one axis the error is the maximum over lines, not their sum. The paper argues that the axis map acts independently on lines, so the maximum of the line errors gives p^2 per axis, and composing d axes gives dp^2.
